correctness.rationale: In the ideal homogeneous Glover–Balmer step-response model K_i(t)=erfc(alpha_i/sqrt(t)), exact pulse superposition yields D_NF−D_FN=Q[G(z)−G(rz)] with z=alpha_1/sqrt(Delta), r=d_2/d_1>1, and G(z)=erfc(z/sqrt(2))−2erfc(z). G has a unique strict maximum at sqrt(3 log 2), since G′=(4e^(−z²)−sqrt(2)e^(−z²/2))/sqrt(pi). For each r>1, G(z)−G(rz) switches exactly once on (z0/r,z0), where its derivative is positive; hence the optimal order reverses once. Implicit differentiation gives strictly decreasing z_r versus r, and the limits bound Delta_c/alpha_1² between 1/(3log2) and 1/z_p². Independently checked the superposition and sign at sample durations for five r-values; finite tests supplement the analytic proof.
